# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Deaf says: I see a display showing 0, a red light, and an embossed sign that reads DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. There are three wires: 1 is red, 2 is green, 3 is yellow.

Deaf can see and has shared colors and a visible sign that says "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE" — but Deaf spoke, which means only Mute can hear it (I'm Blind, and Deaf's speech goes to Mute, not to me... wait, let me check channels).

Actually checking rules: "When you speak, Mute receives it." That's for me (Blind). For Deaf, I need to think about what Deaf's channels are — the turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf, and whatever Deaf sends reaches "whoever comes after" in turn order, but Deaf is last, so Deaf's message reaches next round's Mute (first).

But here in my VIEWABLE CONTEXT, I directly received "Deaf says: ...". So apparently I can hear Deaf's speech too. That's valuable info: sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, display shows 0, red light, wires are red/green/yellow.

This is critical - the sign explicitly says not to cut any wire. I should not act rashly. I need to wait for Mute to read the manual, since Mute might have crucial instructions that override or clarify this. I should not cut anything yet.

```
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has been gesturing to me. So far I have received these symbols in order: peace-sign, peace-sign, index-finger-up, then earlier peace-sign, index-finger-up, peace-sign, peace-sign, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, and before that palm, peace-sign, thumbs-up, palm, index-finger-up, peace-sign, thumbs-up, love-you-gesture, fist. I don't know what they mean yet.

Let me think about this. Deaf received gestures from Mute (since gestures go to Deaf and Mute both, but Mute doesn't receive their own gestures obviously - Deaf sees them). Deaf is relaying to me what gestures Mute made, but Deaf doesn't know what they mean since gestures aren't inherently meaningful without context.

I need to wait for Mute to actually speak to me directly, since Mute's speech reaches me (Blind). Mute reading the manual should give me actual instructions via speech, not through Deaf relaying gestures (which I can't interpret without more context anyway).

Let me note: Deaf cannot hear Mute's speech at all (Mute is mute - cannot speak!). So Mute can only communicate via gesture. Gestures reach Deaf and me? Wait - checking my own channels: "When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." That's mine. For Mute: "Mute: Read the manual... Cannot: Speak" - so Mute can only gesture, not speak.

So Mute's only channel is gesture, which goes to whoever can see - that's Deaf only (I'm Blind, I don't receive gestures). So I never directly get Mute's gestures. Deaf received them and is now relaying via speech to me, translating blank gestures as symbols since Deaf can see them.

So this is the only way information flows to me: Deaf sees Mute's gestures and speaks the symbol names to me. I need to figure out what these symbols encode - likely wire cut positions or a sequence/code.

Let me note the sequence in order received by Deaf so far (chronological):
Round1: palm, peace-sign, thumbs-up, palm, index-finger-up, peace-sign, thumbs-up, love-you-gesture, fist
Round2: peace-sign, index-finger-up, peace-sign, thumbs-up, thumbs-up
Round3: peace-sign, peace-sign, index-finger-up

This looks like it could be encoding letters or numbers per wire. I need more context - possibly Mute is spelling out instructions letter by letter using gesture-to-letter mapping, or numbers via finger count. I should wait for more and ask Deaf to keep relaying, and also ask Deaf what the manual instructions seem to spell out.

I'll ask Deaf to continue relaying and also ask if Mute has indicated anything about which wire is safe.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I can't see your gestures directly - Deaf is relaying them to me as symbol names but I don't have a codebook yet. Can you gesture simple counts like one two three finger to indicate a wire number, or repeat slowly so Deaf can relay clearly which wire to cut")
wait()
```
